---
title: Playground execution image
description: Build and qualify the shared eleven-language Linux image for hosted Playground.
---

## Build and qualify the exact image

Use the Dockerfile in `apps/playground-execution/container` from the reviewed
source commit. Run the build and template checks on an admitted Linux CI
executor with Docker and Node.js 24 or newer.

```sh
(
  set -eu
  image_id_file="$(mktemp)"
  trap 'rm -f "$image_id_file"' 0
  docker build --platform linux/amd64 --iidfile "$image_id_file" \
    apps/playground-execution/container
  node apps/playground-execution/verify-image.mjs "$(cat "$image_id_file")"
)
```

The fixture uses the same stock commands that Meet and Learn load. It checks
Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C, C++, Java, Rust, Go, Ruby, PHP, and Shell.
Each template runs in a fresh local container with UID and GID 65534, all
capabilities removed, no new privileges, no network, a read-only root, and
bounded writable directories. The Dockerfile uses a pinned amd64 base manifest and signed, dated Debian
snapshots. Refresh the base and snapshots together when updating toolchains.
The image contains no application credentials.

Record the source SHA, build invocation, result for every language, and image
ID. After an approved registry upload, also record the Cloudflare registry
digest. Use the digest in the Worker image configuration. The local image ID
and the registry manifest digest identify different objects. Retain the
previous digest while it is a rollback target. [Cloudflare image management](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/guides/image-management/)

## Hosted qualification

Run the fixture again against the digest on the actual Cloudflare execution
path before enabling product traffic. Prove the guest has no external DNS,
direct IP, or private network egress. Check effective UID and GID, all Linux
capability sets, no new privileges, filesystem write bounds, resource limits,
command timeout, output truncation, cancellation, and descendant cleanup.
Confirm the container stops after idle. Measure cold latency and, if the
per-run isolation boundary supports reuse, measure warm latency with a clean
workspace. Include a second participant's result from a real Meet room for
each language.

A Docker fixture verifies the image and template contracts. Cloudflare applies
its own runtime policy. In particular, Durable Object scheduling does not
remove root capabilities merely because an exec process sets a numeric user.
Require hosted isolation evidence before enabling an execution route. [Cloudflare Container exec](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/api/durable-object-container/#exec)

## Cloudflare admission and rollback

The Cloudflare path uses a dedicated Worker, a SQLite coordination Durable
Object, and at most 20 slot Durable Objects that can start guests. Meet keeps
its existing authorization and passes a short-lived capability for the exact
saved revision. The slot uses that capability to download source from Web.
The source-signing key stays in the application servers. The guest receives
only the saved files, command, and stdin.

The Meet adapter is selected only when
`MEET_PLAYGROUND_EXECUTION_PROVIDER=cloudflare`. The Durable Object starts
with admission paused. The ingress and operator secrets are separate.
Production deployment, registry upload, secret installation and
admission changes each require operator authorization for the exact operation.

| Configuration | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `PLAYGROUND_MAX_CONCURRENT` | 20 active slots |
| `PLAYGROUND_MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_USER` | 1 active Run per requester |
| `PLAYGROUND_MAX_RUNS_PER_USER_10_MINUTES` | 30 starts per requester in a rolling 10-minute window |
| `PLAYGROUND_MAX_STARTS_PER_UTC_DAY` | 5,000 starts per UTC day |

Set the values lower for an early deployment. The defaults are also the approved
ceilings. A duplicate request uses the original receipt and consumes no further
start allowance. A failed or ambiguous dispatch consumes its original allowance.
The active project limit protects shared rooms where two participants can ask to
run the same revision. The current Meet adapter handles Run, Stop and Console
results. File changes use the existing collaborative merge and revision-checked
Drive checkpoint. Preview and Learn retain their current provider. Qualify the
writeback and concurrent editor behavior before production activation. Verify
that the legacy runner pool has no eligible Playground capacity while Meet uses
Cloudflare and Learn still uses the legacy provider.

The operator calls `POST /control` with the operator credential and
`{"enabled":false}`. The response records the new generation and the number of
active reservations. Admission then refuses new work. A draining response uses
HTTP 202. A claimed Drive writeback keeps the reservation active until the
coordinator receives the checkpoint confirmation, or until 60 seconds after the
job deadline. That grace covers one room checkpoint and its settlement calls;
after it the Run fails without a saved revision and releases its slot, user and
project, so a lost settlement cannot wedge capacity or block re-enabling. Stop fences new writes
and lets an in-flight export finish its bounded receipt wait. Confirm there are zero
active reservations and zero running instances before rolling back the
application route or rotating service secrets. The same control request is
idempotent. Re-enable only after a scoped approval and verified teardown.
Keep the result endpoint available for existing cloud run receipts while
switching the Meet adapter back to its previous provider.

An accepted reservation schedules finite work. The normal path makes one
assignment RPC, one source fetch with an eight-second timeout, one guest
start, one command, one finalization, and at most one file export. The slot journals its start before
fetching source. Interrupted execution is reconciled without launching the
command again. Cleanup makes at most three attempts per reservation. If
cleanup stays unconfirmed, the slot remains occupied for operator
reconciliation. Clients stop polling at the run deadline. Terminal jobs clear their deadline work. Result polling
uses only the journal. A new admission prunes up to 64 expired receipts.

The Node tests in `apps/playground-execution/src` pin these counts.
`admission.test.mjs` covers the ledger: statements per reservation, restart
deduplication, daily and rolling limits, the pause fence and the cleanup
budget. `slot.test.mjs` covers the slot: the normal path's fetch, start,
command and storage writes, no replay after a restart in the started phase,
an unconfirmed teardown that keeps the slot occupied, and Stop or pause before
the guest starts. `container-run.test.mjs` covers the guest: egress disabled,
output bounds and confirmed destruction. Run them with
`bun run --cwd apps/playground-execution test`.

## Launcher behaviour

The trusted launcher (`container/run.py`) runs as root only to mount a fresh
`/tmp` and build the sandbox. It first runs the same namespace, privilege drop
and Landlock chain around `/bin/true`; if the kernel or runtime cannot provide
any part of it, the Run fails as `sandbox_failed` before user code runs. The
program then runs as UID and GID 65534 with no capabilities, no new
privileges, an empty network namespace, its own PID namespace and writes limited to
`/tmp`.

After a normal exit the launcher exports the workspace as a complete
inventory. Files the program created that cannot be saved (binaries, names
outside the path rules, files over 256 KiB, non-UTF-8 text) are left out. If a
project file still exists but cannot be saved, or the workspace exceeds the
inventory or size limits, nothing is exported and the Run keeps its output.
An export problem never replaces the program's output.

## Usage and cost

The initial instance size is 0.5 vCPU, 4 GiB of memory, and an 8 GB disk.
The command has a 30-second timeout within a 50-second job deadline. Output
is capped at 64 KiB. Fresh instances are destroyed after execution, with a
15-second inactivity timeout as a fallback. Warm reuse requires independent
hosted qualification before use.

At published overage rates, the estimated Containers cost is
`$0.00001056 × live seconds + $0.000020 × active vCPU-seconds`.

| Modeled Run | Live seconds | Active vCPU-seconds | Cost per Run | Cost at 150,000 Runs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Cold | 45 | 5 | $0.0005752 | $86.28 |
| Warm, conditional | 25 | 2.5 | $0.0003140 | $47.10 |
| Stress scenario | 70 | 35 | $0.0014392 | $215.88 |

A 15-second idle tail costs about $0.0001584 per instance plus actual CPU.
Sleeping container compute is $0. The estimates exclude the Workers Paid
base charge, Workers and Durable Object requests, duration, SQLite storage,
and logs, and are before shared included allowances. The stress scenario
is an estimate. Provider shutdown latency can change billed usage. Record
real cold-start and shutdown times, journal operation counts, and actual
usage during qualification. [Cloudflare Containers pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/pricing/) · [Workers and Durable Objects pricing](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/)
